minutes.headline: Board warns FY27's balanced-budget scenario would eliminate the recreation director and close the town beach
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission got updates on the skate park, a possible new use of the Marshall T-ball field, and partnered with the Lunenburg Business Association to run the 2026 vendor fair, including a possible dunk-tank rental. The chair also laid out how the town's proposed FY27 balanced budget versus two override tiers would affect the recreation director position and town beach operations, and the board approved minutes with one correction.

votes.motion: Authorize a partnership with the Lunenburg Business Association for the 2026 vendor fair with the understanding that no municipal staff support will be provided.
Book/spend money to rent the dunk tank sooner than the next meeting if necessary.
Approve the minutes for January 28th and February 3rd with the correction that the commission itself did not call local pools.

budget_items.what_was_said: Under the balanced budget, the recreation director position would be eliminated and the town beach salary line would decrease, leaving no funds to operate the beach next summer with town funds.
Tier one would keep the recreation director as a part-time employee, increase the beach salary line, and restore a small programming budget.
Tier two would fund a full-time recreation director and carries the same beach salary line as tier one.

The chair had the town accountant identify the vendor (a company in Shirley); a one-day rental was described as roughly four hundred dollars with a cheaper-per-day two-day rental option, and the board planned to get exact numbers before deciding.

budget_items.topic: T-ball per-player fee at Marshall field
budget_items.what_was_said: Use of the Marshall T-ball field would normally carry the same per-player fee charged for other players, but the commission discussed possibly waiving it if the league helps clean up the field.

decisions.decision: Facility staff will get a price from Lakeview for prepping the Marshall T-ball field, and the baseball program may help with the work.
If the T-ball field starts being used, dogs will need to be prohibited there again; the facility director can make that call day-to-day ahead of a formal commission vote.
The chair will get exact dunk-tank rental numbers and pricing for one-day versus two-day/rain-date rental before the next meeting.

what_happened.line: Under the town's proposed FY27 balanced budget, the recreation director position would be eliminated and beach funding cut, closing the town beach next summer.
Two override tiers were outlined: one restores a part-time director and some programming, the other funds a full-time director; both keep the beach open.
The board voted to partner with the Lunenburg Business Association to run the 2026 vendor fair, with no town staff support provided.
The board voted to authorize renting a dunk tank for the fair before the next meeting if needed.
Facility staff will price prepping the Marshall T-ball field for possible use, with a dog-ban decision to follow if it is opened up.

why_it_matters: The FY27 balanced-budget scenario would end the town beach and the recreation director job, a service and a position that would return only if voters approve an override.
Residents will be asked to choose among a no-override, part-time-director, or full-time-director budget path that decides what recreation programming exists next year.
The vendor-fair partnership hands event logistics to the business association rather than town staff, which limits what municipal resources back the event.
